fingerprints.story:
The sea was a sheet of hammered pewter under a sky the colour of old bone. For forty years, Elias had watched it from the lantern room of the St. Jude’s Point lighthouse, a solitary sentinel against the ceaseless churn of the Atlantic. His world was one of polished brass, the scent of whale oil, and the rhythmic, comforting tick-tock of the great clock that powered the light. It was a life of predictable, mechanical grace.
